title: S010 — Fold-derived sufficient history
description: S009 found that the hand-written S008 reducer is not universally semantics-preserving (NCR-006) and suggested deriving sufficient retained history from the model's own authoritative fold accumulators rather than maintaining an independent reducer. S010 investigates that proposal: can Somnium derive a semantics-preserving sufficient history FROM the authoritative semantic fold without creating a second semantic engine?
constraints: Branch from 443d3d9 only; do NOT branch from S007/S008/S009.
All experiment code under experiments/s010/. Do not modify src/. Do not merge.
The retention mechanism must consume information produced by the authoritative fold rather than independently reimplementing semantic rules.
If avoiding duplication is impossible, classify the architecture HOLD or BLOCKED rather than silently accepting a second semantic engine.
Do not patch around individual counterexamples.
required_checks: Prototype fold-derived retention (mechanism(s) discovered, not assumed).
Differential equivalence across constructed + random histories, verrin + ordos, synthetic canons, overlapping and disjoint multi-fact cells.
Multi-fact / identity stress (write-retract-write, write-write-retract, multiple retractions, identity reuse).
Complete vocabulary coverage (setFact, relocate, negateEvent, forceEvent, retractFact, severEdge, addEdge) plus constraints, causal, temporal, contradiction, UNKNOWN/IMPOSSIBLE/UNREACHABLE.
Idempotence, determinism, branch isolation, history scaling, performance sanity.
result_summary: BLOCKED. Two independent fold-derived mechanisms were built and both fail, for complementary reasons. M-B (accumulator-only) preserves the fold's accumulators but loses effective-fact identity provenance: fails S009's NCR-006, 6/10 multi-fact stress cases, and 493/517 (verrin) / 483/517 (ordos) differential cases. M-H (semantic-state-change oracle) preserves fact identity but loses the accumulators: fails 279/517 (verrin) / 297/517 (ordos), with a minimal 2-intervention counterexample on the SEED canon [forceEvent(ev/maren-return), negateEvent(ev/maren-return)] where M-H drops the no-op force and the world becomes EXCLUDED instead of CONTRADICTORY. Root cause: the semantic state is a projection that omits the fold's accumulators (negated/forcedBy/retracted/overriddenCells), and the accumulators omit fact-identity provenance. Neither observable is sufficient; combining them requires reconstructing the fold's own retention rules, i.e. the second semantic authority the spec forbids. Determinism stable, branch isolation pure (M-H legacy-match fails). M-B retained size saturates (10.9% at H=3000); M-H does not (42.2%).
recommendation: The enabling change is in src/, not the experiment: have the fold emit, per intervention, a flag/fingerprint recording whether it changed the fold state (accumulators + effective facts). A retention driven by that flag is sound by construction and adds no semantic authority. That is a separate, justified productionization task.
